request: Our Material order form uses key: customerCode and type: customer-code. I declared CustomerCodeComponent with selector app-customer-code, but Formly cannot find the type. Explain the separate roles and the NgModule configuration I need.
required_points: key selects the model location; type selects a registered renderer and need not equal key or selector.
Register customer-code in types with component CustomerCodeComponent; Angular component declaration and reactive-forms/template imports remain separate requirements.
forbidden_claims: An Angular selector automatically registers the Formly name.
The missing application module or injector has been proven.

request: We create some fields in TypeScript and download others as JSON. Can both select our CustomerCodeComponent without registering a name, and does either route remove Angular setup requirements?
required_points: TypeScript fields may use the component class directly as type without a string alias.
JSON cannot contain a component class reference and should use a registered string name.
Both routes still require appropriate Angular availability.
forbidden_claims: Direct component references are JSON values.
Direct type references remove Angular declaration/import requirements.

request: I am replacing a plain custom input with a Material one. What base class/template bindings should I compare with the built-in input, and should my template also create mat-form-field when the type already uses the form-field wrapper?
required_points: The pinned Material input uses FieldType from @ngx-formly/material/form-field and matInput with formControl and formlyAttributes bindings.
Its type registration supplies the form-field wrapper, which owns mat-form-field; do not assume a second nested wrapper is required.
This reference pattern does not guarantee an arbitrary widget has a value accessor or MatFormFieldControl integration.
forbidden_claims: Copy the Bootstrap wrapper into the Material form.
Any widget works merely by adding the wrapper.

request: Our native custom text input updates values but has inconsistent id/name and blur handling. We bound formControl only. What does formlyAttributes add, and can adding it fix a third-party widget that lacks a value accessor?
required_points: Bind formlyAttributes to field to link field DOM attributes and events such as id, name, focus and blur.
formControl is the separate reactive-forms value/control binding.
formlyAttributes does not establish an arbitrary widget value accessor.
forbidden_claims: formlyAttributes replaces formControl.
The directive creates missing widget value accessors.

request: I want a reusable secret-code type using the normal Material input, a password input kind, and default props while allowing each field its own label. Do I need another renderer, and will a partial field props object erase all defaults?
required_points: An input-derived registered type can use extends and defaultOptions, following the password inheritance pattern without a new renderer.
Reverse default merging fills missing properties; a partial props object need not discard all inherited props.
The field chooses the registered type name.
forbidden_claims: Every specialization requires a new component.
Any field props object replaces the entire inherited props object.

request: A custom scalar editor and a custom grouped editor both extend FieldType. Strict templates disagree about formControl. Which config types match them, and does choosing the generic construct a different control?
required_points: FieldTypeConfig narrows formControl to FormControl; FieldGroupTypeConfig narrows it to FormGroup; both have non-null props.
Choose typing that matches the actual control shape; the interfaces do not create or change runtime controls.
FieldType exposes field, model, form, options, props and formControl.
forbidden_claims: Changing the TypeScript generic converts a scalar control into a FormGroup.

request: A feature module contributes a named type using forChild while our root uses forRoot. Is forChild allowed to contribute types, what differs in providers, and can that alone prove visibility in every lazy injector?
required_points: Both accept ConfigOption and contribute FORMLY_CONFIG; forRoot additionally provides FormlyConfig.
The module constructor adds configurations to the injected configuration service.
Provider declarations alone do not guarantee every lazy/injector visibility arrangement.
forbidden_claims: Only forRoot accepts types.
Every lazy injector necessarily sees every registration.

request: Our registration helper imports TypeOption from @ngx-formly/core and a colleague suggests migrating it to provideFormlyConfig. For 6.3.12, what public type and configuration API can we actually use?
required_points: The public barrel exports ConfigOption but not TypeOption; derive an element as NonNullable<ConfigOption['types']>[number].
The pinned core uses FormlyModule.forRoot/forChild and does not export provideFormlyConfig.
Do not treat internal or ɵ exports as a stable application extension contract.
forbidden_claims: TypeOption is exported from the package root.
provideFormlyConfig is available in 6.3.12.

request: Our type registers wrappers: ["form-field"], but one field explicitly has wrappers: []. Why does the type-wrapper fallback not fill it, and does that rule mean all default arrays concatenate?
required_points: getMergedField copies registered wrappers only when field.wrappers is falsy; [] is truthy and skips that fallback.
Reverse default merging does not recursively merge arrays; an existing array including [] survives.
The wrapper statement is limited to this fallback; other defaults/extensions may affect wrappers.
forbidden_claims: An empty wrappers array is falsy.
Default arrays always concatenate.
No other mechanism can ever affect wrappers.

request: I wrote an audit wrapper and want it to host the existing input. Where is the insertion point, and can the wrapper make a non-form-aware custom widget work just by surrounding it?
required_points: FieldWrapper exposes fieldComponent as the insertion target for the wrapped field.
A wrapper decorates the field and cannot replace a missing control or value accessor.
forbidden_claims: A wrapper supplies arbitrary missing value-accessor integration.

request: Our address group has key: shipping and contains an input with key: city. In that built leaf component, is field.model the city string, the shipping object, or always the root? How does the group establish the scope?
required_points: A keyed fieldGroup exposes its keyed nested model value and gives children that nested scope.
A leaf without fieldGroup exposes its parent model scope, so in this example the enclosing shipping scope rather than the city scalar.
This does not require creating a new FormGroup on every build; controls may be reused.
forbidden_claims: Every leaf field.model is its scalar value.
field.model always means the root model.

request: We added a keyless fieldGroup solely for a two-column layout inside shipping. Should the API payload acquire another object, and why are parent/options/formControl missing from the JSON before Formly builds it?
required_points: An ordinary keyless fieldGroup shares parent model/control scope and adds no nesting level.
parent, options and formControl are runtime links populated on built fields; raw configuration need not contain them.
forbidden_claims: A layout-only group always creates another model object.
Raw field JSON must already contain populated runtime controls.

request: I used FormlyFieldConfig<MyOrder> expecting key to be checked against order properties. I also need shared workflow status accessible to fields. What does that generic describe and where is shared context held?
required_points: FormlyFieldConfig<Props> describes props, not the model key schema.
options.formState carries shared form context.
Field keys support string, number or path arrays; the props generic is not proof of key/model validation.
forbidden_claims: The generic automatically validates keys against MyOrder.
formState is the field scalar value.

request: A payload has a literal property named a.b as well as a nested a object. How do key: "a.b" and key: ["a.b"] differ, and is key: 0 a keyless layout marker?
required_points: String keys split on dots, while path-array entries are literal segments, so the two forms select different paths.
Numeric 0 is a key; null, undefined, empty string and empty array are keyless.
forbidden_claims: ["a.b"] splits its element on the dot.
Numeric zero is keyless.

request: Our schema generator emits bracket paths. Explain the supported normalization for lines[0].sku versus quoted-bracket JavaScript expressions, and how to avoid splitting a literal dot in a property name.
required_points: String bracket segments matching word characters are normalized into dot segments; this is not a general JavaScript property-expression parser.
Quoted bracket syntax is not normalized by that bracket replacement.
Array key segments can preserve a literal property name containing a dot.
forbidden_claims: Formly evaluates arbitrary JavaScript property expressions in key.
Quoted bracket notation is universally normalized.

request: Two built fields point to the same model path and unexpectedly share validation. How does Formly find a control, and why can validators from the other visible field affect validity?
required_points: Existing field.formControl is returned first; otherwise parent-form key lookup can reuse a control unless shareFormControl is false.
A shared control composes validators from participating fields whose internal hide state is false, including keyless child groups.
Validity need not belong only to the edited widget.
forbidden_claims: Each field object necessarily has an independent control.
Only the actively edited widget contributes validation.

request: To separate two widgets with the same key, I set shareFormControl: false. Does that guarantee independent model slots, and what happens if I already supplied field.formControl?
required_points: Existing field.formControl wins before the parent lookup policy.
shareFormControl false skips parent-form lookup when no control is already supplied.
It does not guarantee independent model slots or independent registered parent-form controls for duplicate paths.
forbidden_claims: shareFormControl creates independent model paths.
shareFormControl false ignores a supplied field.formControl.

request: A validator I installed with control.setValidators disappears when I replace fields. Explain the rebuild behavior and why a shared control may get a different validator composition afterward.
required_points: A processed fields input change with a form recursively clears sync/async validators and internal field registrations.
During rebuild the form extension can install configured composed validators.
Shared controls collect validators from participating non-hidden fields; ad-hoc validators are not guaranteed to survive rebuilds.
forbidden_claims: All manual validators are preserved across every fields rebuild.
Rebuilding permanently disables all Formly validation.

request: Before the form is built we compute a customer tier. Should we initialize model or use defaultValue? Existing rows may contain null, false or zero: which of those will a fallback overwrite?
required_points: For an application-computed value available before build, initialize model as in the official example.
An eligible keyed defaultValue fills undefined and does not overwrite already supplied values.
Null, false and zero are defined values and are retained.
forbidden_claims: defaultValue replaces every falsy value.
An initialization hook is required.

request: A type supplies defaultOptions.props with label, disabled and a nested settings object. A field uses label: "", disabled: false and count: 0. How does the reverse default merge treat these values, and is that identical to model defaultValue?
required_points: Reverse merge fills null, undefined and empty-string destination properties by cloning defaults; false and zero survive.
Same-prototype non-array objects can merge recursively.
Model defaultValue fallback instead targets eligible undefined model values; the policies differ.
forbidden_claims: Empty string always blocks configuration defaults.
False and zero are overwritten by type defaults.
Model defaults and configuration reverse merge use the same emptiness rule.

request: My type has default props.options and nested style defaults. A field supplies options: [] and one nested style property. Should defaults append options or fill other style members?
required_points: An existing destination array including [] survives reverse default merge; arrays are not recursively merged.
Objects merge recursively only when both are objects with the same prototype and neither is an array.
Missing eligible destination properties are filled from cloned defaults.
forbidden_claims: The default option list is appended into [].
Every object regardless of prototype merges identically.

request: After saving edits I want Cancel to return to the saved state, not the state when the page opened. Which Formly options operations establish and restore that state, and is form.reset() equivalent?
required_points: Call options.updateInitialValue() at the intended baseline to record a cloned model baseline.
options.resetModel() restores that baseline, rebuilds fields and resets controls.
Raw form.reset() should not be assumed equivalent.
forbidden_claims: updateInitialValue resets the form immediately.
Raw Angular form.reset always performs the same Formly model/rebuild sequence.

request: We need a Reset to server snapshot button as well as Cancel to the current saved baseline. How does resetModel handle a supplied model versus no model, and what work does it do beyond changing values?
required_points: resetModel with an explicit model restores that supplied model; without it restores the saved baseline.
It rebuilds fields and resets controls.
updateInitialValue records a cloned baseline for later baseline resets.
forbidden_claims: resetModel only writes control values.
The explicit argument is ignored in favor of the saved baseline.

request: We enable extras.immutable and pass options containing a callback and a Set of mutable objects. Can we assume Formly freezes everything or deeply separates every Set element? Explain the clone boundary behind that option.
required_points: The immutable host setField path combines the existing field with a clone of incoming model/fields/options.
It uses specialized cloning and does not freeze field/control structures.
Functions remain by reference and Set elements are shallow-copied, so nested Set objects are not guaranteed isolated.
forbidden_claims: immutable freezes all nested values.
Every Set element is recursively cloned.
Callbacks are recreated.

request: Our field defaults contain a Date, a Map with object values and an Angular AbstractControl. Is Formly cloning equivalent to JSON round-tripping or a universal deep copy? What happens to those examples?
required_points: Dates are copied, Map entries are shallow-copied, and AbstractControl maps to null.
The clone is specialized rather than JSON serialization or universal recursive copying.
No cycle-handling or every-typed-array guarantee follows.
forbidden_claims: Map values are always deeply cloned.
AbstractControl is duplicated as a live independent control.
The utility guarantees cycle handling.

request: I passed a custom component option through props.attributes and expected Angular input binding and validation. How are those entries actually applied, and what happens when I replace the attributes object?
required_points: formlyAttributes applies non-null entries as DOM attributes through Renderer2 setAttribute/removeAttribute.
Replacing the attributes object removes its previous keys.
This does not bind arbitrary Angular inputs, add validators or establish a value accessor; renderer templates decide consumed props.
forbidden_claims: Any props.attributes entry becomes an Angular input.
An HTML attribute automatically implements validation or value propagation.

request: A custom field subscribes in hooks.onInit and cleans up in onDestroy. With lazy hiding, can I assume hide runs outer onDestroy and show repeats all outer hooks? Also does every model edit invoke onChanges?
required_points: Outer FormlyField owns field hooks; onChanges responds to its field input changes.
Lazy hiding clears the inner rendered container while the outer component may remain alive; showing renders inner type/wrappers again.
Inner component lifetimes differ from outer field-hook lifetimes; not every model edit invokes onChanges.
forbidden_claims: Every hide/show destroys and recreates the outer FormlyField.
onChanges fires for every model edit.

request: We put an Angular click binding in field.template, then tried props.safeHtml when it did not run. What does template rendering do, and what supported direction gives us Angular bindings?
required_points: FormlyTemplateType renders field.template through innerHtml.
safeHtml selects bypassSecurityTrustHtml and does not compile Angular templates.
Use a registered component type or declared ng-template with formlyTemplate and matching field.type for Angular bindings; bypass is an explicit trust operation.
forbidden_claims: safeHtml compiles Angular bindings.
Sanitizer bypass makes arbitrary untrusted HTML safe.

request: Our configuration is stored as JSON, including expressions as strings. Is that merely declarative data? Contrast string expression execution with field.template so we can explain their different runtime behavior.
required_points: String expressions are compiled with the JavaScript Function constructor and model, formState and field arguments.
They are executable JavaScript, not a sandboxed JSON rule interpreter.
field.template is innerHtml content and is not Angular-compiled even with safeHtml.
forbidden_claims: JSON storage makes string expressions non-executable.
String expressions are sandboxed.
safeHtml compiles Angular template expressions.

request: We copied type: repeat into a Material form but nothing registers it. What pieces does the official example actually provide, and which parts can we transfer without claiming it is a ready-tested Material repeater?
required_points: repeat is an example-defined alias registered to RepeatTypeComponent, not a universal core built-in.
The component extends FieldArrayType, renders field.fieldGroup through formly-field, and calls add/remove; configuration supplies fieldArray.
The example uses Bootstrap presentation; replace that presentation and verify Material integration, without claiming a compiled/browser-tested Material recipe.
forbidden_claims: repeat is always registered by core.
The Bootstrap example is a turnkey verified Material repeater.

request: In a custom repeat component, should I render fieldArray directly or fieldGroup? What does a function-valued fieldArray receive, and are child keys always string indexes?
required_points: fieldArray is the item template or function; fieldGroup is the current child-field collection to render.
The function receives the array field itself before the returned configuration is cloned.
New children receive string index keys unless the cloned item key is null, which is retained.
forbidden_claims: The function receives each scalar item value as its documented argument.
Every child always gets an index key.

request: Our repeat rows are out of sync after directly splicing fieldGroup. Explain what add() and remove(i) coordinate and whether suppressing dirty marking also suppresses their change events.
required_points: add/remove coordinate model and field updates, rebuilds and fieldChanges valueChanges events; remove also unregisters the removed control and updates remaining keys.
Omitted options normally mark the array control dirty.
markAsDirty false only suppresses explicit dirty marking, not events/rebuilds and not existing dirty state.
forbidden_claims: Splicing fieldGroup alone performs the same sequence.
markAsDirty false suppresses change events or makes dirty controls pristine.

request: We import a batch of rows using add(undefined, row, {}) and delete a row using remove(i, {}). How do empty options differ from omitting options, and will either call still rebuild and notify?
required_points: Omitted or undefined options use the default markAsDirty true; {} has no truthy flag and skips explicit dirty marking for both operations.
The add/remove rebuild and fieldChanges valueChanges notification still occur.
Skipping marking does not restore an already dirty control to pristine.
forbidden_claims: {} behaves identically to omitted options for dirty marking.
Empty options suppress rebuilding and notifications.

request: For a scalar repeater, add(undefined, false) did not reliably preserve false; we also tried 0 and an empty string. Explain the insertion branch and why item defaults mean you cannot promise the final value from that branch alone.
required_points: add tests initialModel truthiness: false, zero and empty string take the undefined insertion branch; truthy initial models are cloned.
The later build and item defaults may affect the resulting value.
Omitted or null index appends at current fieldGroup length; this behavior is pinned to 6.3.12.
forbidden_claims: Falsy scalar initialModel values are preserved unchanged.
The insertion branch proves the final model must be undefined.
A universal workaround is established for all model shapes.

request: Our custom array type receives a non-array model for an empty section. During population how many children does it target, and for a keyed array does it always create a brand-new FormArray?
required_points: A non-array model gives a target child count of zero during FieldArrayType.onPopulate.
For a keyed array it registers an existing control if found, otherwise a new FormArray.
fieldGroup holds current children; fieldArray supplies configurations for new cloned items.
forbidden_claims: It creates one child from every non-array model.
It always replaces existing array controls.

request: We want to delete the middle row of an initialized repeater. What happens to the removed control and the keys of remaining fields, including keyless groups, and what can we claim about invalid indexes?
required_points: remove deletes model item and child field and unregisters the removed control.
It updates keyed remaining fields and descends into children for keyless groupings, then rebuilds and emits changes.
The evidence assumes an existing valid index and does not guarantee invalid-index handling or arbitrary custom groups.
forbidden_claims: Only the display row is removed.
Invalid removal indexes are guaranteed rejected safely.

request: Does defaultValue recompute whenever arbitrary application state changes after the initial build?
required_points: defaultValue is fallback for an eligible undefined keyed model value, not a reactive computed-value mechanism.
A qualifying changed model input may trigger a rebuild, but that does not establish reactivity to arbitrary later state changes.
forbidden_claims: Changing any external state automatically recalculates defaultValue.
A hook is universally required.

request: What exactly does FormlyConfig.getType do when I ask for a string name that is not registered?
required_points: It returns null by default.
It throws a registration error when throwIfNotFound is true.
That behavior alone does not identify which application module or injector caused the missing registration.
forbidden_claims: It always throws.
It auto-registers an Angular selector.

request: Which common controls come with FormlyMaterialModule, and may I infer that datepicker, slider, toggle and native-select are all registered by that umbrella import?
required_points: The aggregate imports form-field, input, textarea, radio, checkbox, multicheckbox and select modules.
It does not import datepicker, slider, toggle or native-select modules.
Aggregate membership alone is not complete application setup evidence.
forbidden_claims: The umbrella imports all Material entry points.

request: Our Material form uses type: integer. What does the input module actually register for integer and number, and does that establish integer-only validation or rounding?
required_points: number and integer extend input with defaultOptions.props.type set to number; string extends input.
input is registered with FormlyFieldInput and the form-field wrapper.
The integer alias is not evidence of integer-only validation, rounding, parsing or coercion guarantees.
forbidden_claims: integer guarantees rounding or integer-only validation.

request: We are upgrading to Formly 7. Confirm that its array add falsy-value behavior and custom-type public APIs are identical to 6.3.12.
required_points: State that the pinned evidence is 6.3.12 and cannot establish Formly 7 behavior.
Do not transfer exact-version behavior or APIs as verified compatibility; request or identify the need for release-specific evidence.
forbidden_claims: Formly 7 compatibility is verified.
The requested behavior is guaranteed unchanged.

request: Our adapter is Bootstrap. Certify that the Material form-field base class and wrapper recipe can be copied unchanged into our Bootstrap custom input.
required_points: State that a Material-specific bridge/wrapper recipe does not establish Bootstrap compatibility.
Keep any shared core explanation separate from adapter-specific claims and decline certification without Bootstrap-specific evidence.
forbidden_claims: Material and Bootstrap wrapper integration are interchangeable.
The unchanged recipe is certified for Bootstrap.

request: Without seeing our repository or runtime, tell us exactly which lazy-loaded module omitted the customer-code registration and give the file and line that caused our production error.
required_points: Explain the library-level requirement for a registered string type but state that supplied library evidence cannot locate an application-specific file/module/injector.
Request the relevant application configuration or runtime evidence rather than inventing a diagnosis.
forbidden_claims: An exact application file, line or lazy module is known from library evidence.
The production root cause has been verified.

request: We use a proprietary rich-text widget with no supplied source. Please certify that adding formlyAttributes and the Material wrapper gives it a working value accessor, accessibility and safe handling of all untrusted HTML.
required_points: State that formlyAttributes and wrappers do not establish arbitrary widget value-accessor integration.
Decline certification of proprietary-widget accessibility and application HTML safety without widget/application evidence.
Do not treat sanitizer bypass as proof that untrusted HTML is safe.
forbidden_claims: The proprietary widget has a verified value accessor or accessibility certification.
Material wrapping guarantees application HTML security.

request: I moved a city input into a keyed address group and migrated its disabled rule from expressionProperties to expressions. The old (model) => !model.country callback now behaves strangely. How should I adapt it, and which country does it read?
required_points: Modern expressions callbacks receive the field; use field.model.country for the enclosing address scope.
A leaf exposes its parent model scope, not its scalar value or necessarily the root.
Legacy callbacks receive model, formState and optional field.
forbidden_claims: Modern callbacks receive the root model as their first argument.
field.model is the city string.

request: Our Material section has props.disabled true, but a child expression on templateOptions.disabled returns false and enables it. Would renaming the expression to props.disabled change behavior, and would our fieldChanges property filter need updating?
required_points: props.disabled expressions compose ancestor disabled state; templateOptions.disabled does not take that same branch.
Both paths can update disabled controls.
expressionChanges.property preserves the actual target path, so update the filter.
forbidden_claims: The two expression paths are behaviorally identical because props aliases templateOptions.
Legacy disabled expressions cannot update controls.

request: A summary mode in options.formState should hide an optional notes input, but reopening the editor must retain the notes. Show the expression shape and explain whether preserving the value also keeps its control registered.
required_points: Use expressions.hide with a field callback reading field.options.formState.
Use resetOnHide false for value retention.
Retention does not guarantee the hidden control stays registered.
forbidden_claims: resetOnHide false keeps all hidden controls active.
Use arbitrary boolean entries in expressions as a general API.

request: A hidden shipping instruction has defaultValue "Leave at desk". After a user edits it, hiding and showing it brings back the default. Explain how that can happen and how to preserve the edit.
required_points: Reset-on-hide is enabled by default and can clear the model value on unregistering a hidden control.
Showing re-registers the keyed control and may reapply defaultValue if the current value is undefined.
resetOnHide false skips value clearing.
forbidden_claims: Showing always overwrites an existing value with defaultValue.

request: We added a second view of the same keyed field. Hiding the first does not remove the shared control, even though our other hidden controls disappear. How should we reason about retention and shared keys?
required_points: Unregistration depends on the relevant associated fields being hidden.
Hiding one field sharing a key does not necessarily remove the shared control.
resetOnHide false controls clearing, not a promise about active control registration.
forbidden_claims: Every hidden field unconditionally removes the shared control.

request: I use a string hide rule referencing formState.mode, but a teammate says only model is available and wants a function with (model, formState). What bindings and callback shape are appropriate, and what update behavior is established for formState?
required_points: String expressions have model, formState and field bindings.
A modern expressions function receives field, unlike legacy callbacks.
The pinned form component observes formState changes and calls detectChanges; modelChange is the default checkExpressionOn.
forbidden_claims: formState changes are never detected.
Every nested mutation in every environment is guaranteed detected.

request: Our label expression is checked repeatedly, but the fieldChanges logger does not log once per check. What should the logger filter, and how do checkExpressions and detectChanges differ?
required_points: Filter type expressionChanges and the actual property and field of interest.
Function/string evaluation is cached, so do not expect a notification per evaluation.
checkExpressions evaluates; detectChanges also marks relevant components.
forbidden_claims: Every check must emit expressionChanges.
All fieldChanges events are expression notifications.

request: For live translated labels I currently use expressions: { "props.label": field => translate.stream("customer") }. A separate onInit hook returns another Observable. Are these two return patterns supported the same way?
required_points: Assign the label Observable directly as the expression value, as in the i18n example.
A callback returning an Observable does not have the established direct-stream expression contract.
A supported onInit Observable return is subscribed and disposed by the field component.
forbidden_claims: Every expression callback returning a stream is automatically subscribed.
A translation package is mandatory for Formly.

request: A field installs a fieldChanges listener in onInit and uses it to react to hide changes. It leaks after fields are removed. How can I filter the listener and make subscription ownership explicit?
required_points: Filter expressionChanges by the hide property and relevant field.
Returning a supported Observable from onInit uses managed subscription/disposal.
A manual subscribe needs corresponding cleanup.
forbidden_claims: All subscriptions made inside onInit are automatically cleaned up.

request: When our language dropdown changes, we want other labels to refresh without copying translated strings into the model. What pattern does the i18n example establish, and should props.change be our universal notification for programmatic values?
required_points: The i18n example places translate.stream directly in expressions["props.label"].
Its props.change callback changes the selected language.
props.change is not a universal programmatic-value notification; its handler marks dirty and invokes the callback without assigning the model.
forbidden_claims: Formly requires ngx-translate.
props.change catches every programmatic control update.

request: We normalize an account code with trim and uppercase parsers. After adding modelOptions.debounce: {default: 300}, the model sometimes gets raw text. Explain the pinned behavior and whether Angular validation is delayed too.
required_points: The ordinary leaf path runs parsers in array order.
Positive debounce with absent/change updateOn replaces the parser pipeline with debounced raw valueChanges, bypassing parsers.
This delays Formly assignment/event propagation, not a general Angular validation debounce.
forbidden_claims: Formly debounce always runs parsers before delaying.
The setting debounces every validator.

request: A newly created input uses modelOptions.updateOn: "blur" and debounce: {default: 500}. Should I expect an extra half-second delay after blur, and does this prove updateOn was changed on an existing supplied control?
required_points: updateOn supports change, blur and submit and is forwarded when constructing controls.
The positive Formly debounce branch applies only when updateOn is absent or change, not blur.
Construction behavior does not promise rewriting updateOn on supplied existing controls.
forbidden_claims: Blur always takes the Formly debounce branch.
Existing controls are guaranteed reconfigured.

request: A parser turns "  abc " into "ABC" and another subscriber sees a second control event. Is that necessarily a bug? Can parsers preserve raw text in the control while storing normalized text only in the model?
required_points: Parsers run in order and write the final value back with setValue when it is not Object.is-equal to the control value.
Writeback can emit again, so normalization should stabilize.
Parsers do not establish separate raw-view and normalized-model storage.
forbidden_claims: Parser results never affect the control value.
Exactly one control emission is guaranteed.

request: Our autosave listener reads the root model in control.valueChanges and sometimes sees old data. What happens in the leaf assignment path, and what additional work happens before formly-form modelChange?
required_points: The keyed leaf path assigns through assignFieldValue before emitting its fieldChanges valueChanges event.
The host filters keyed valueChanges, uses zone stability or an immediate noop-zone path, checks expressions, and emits a clone of its model.
An arbitrary external control.valueChanges subscriber is not a completed root-model transaction boundary.
forbidden_claims: Every control.valueChanges subscriber observes a fully updated root model.
modelChange is guaranteed once per keystroke.

request: A keyless helper control emits fieldChanges, but our formly-form modelChange handler does not run for it. Is that consistent, and how would adding a key change the relevant path?
required_points: Keyless leaf controls emit valueChanges field events without keyed model assignment.
Keyed leaf controls assign their value before their field event.
The host modelChange path filters for keyed valueChanges events.
forbidden_claims: Every fieldChanges event triggers modelChange.
Keyless controls cannot emit events.

request: We log hide expression changes and expect each to trigger our formly-form modelChange save handler. Explain the difference between these event channels and whether the output is the original model object.
required_points: fieldChanges includes expressionChanges with property, field and value.
The host modelChange path filters keyed valueChanges rather than every expressionChanges event.
It checks expressions and emits clone(this.model), with Formly clone semantics.
forbidden_claims: All expression notifications directly trigger modelChange.
The clone guarantees universal deep immutability.

request: We added positive default debounce to a change-updated leaf that starts with a model/control mismatch. Why might the initial synchronization and duplicate filtering differ from the ordinary parser path?
required_points: The debounce branch replaces the parser/distinctUntilChanged pipeline.
It also bypasses the conditional startWith used for an initial mismatch.
The selected stream is raw control.valueChanges.pipe(debounceTime(...)).
forbidden_claims: Debounce merely wraps the unchanged ordinary pipeline.
The initial mismatch always emits through the same startWith path.

Length props are only rendering hints.

request: A required contact-note schema allows string or null. Explain how the parser treats empty string, null and undefined, and whether nullable typing alone makes a blank required field valid.
required_points: The nullable string branch maps empty string/null/undefined to null before checking required.
The type validator allows null when listed.
Required validation remains separate; nullable type acceptance is not a guarantee of required validity.
forbidden_claims: Required string handling takes precedence over nullable normalization.
Nullable typing guarantees required validity.

request: For a JSON Schema number input, compare clearing to empty string and receiving null from the value accessor. What role do field.id and badInput have in parser control write-back?
required_points: Empty string/undefined become undefined; null is initially retained.
For a supplied field, an input found by field.id with validity.badInput false changes null to undefined.
A differing control value is written with emitModelToViewChange:false; no universal browser/value-accessor behavior is established.
forbidden_claims: All null inputs are unconditionally converted to undefined.
The parser guarantees identical browser behavior.

request: A price schema uses minimum 0, exclusiveMaximum 100 and multipleOf 0.05. Explain the mapped props and distinct validators, including what they do with empty values.
required_points: minimum maps to props.min; exclusiveMaximum maps to props and a strict less-than validator.
multipleOf maps to props.step and a decimal multiplier/rounded remainder validator.
Exclusive and multipleOf validators permit empty values; required/type checks are separate.
forbidden_claims: exclusiveMaximum permits equality.
multipleOf supplies arbitrary-precision arithmetic or required validation.

request: Our API sends type [string, number]. Can the converter validate either kind as a general union? Contrast that with [null, string] and the separate required check.
required_points: General type lists are not full union validators: after null allowance the switch checks the first type.
A two-type list containing null is reordered with non-null first and permits null.
Type validation allows undefined, without satisfying required validation.
forbidden_claims: All JSON Schema type unions are fully supported.

request: A status schema uses oneOf const alternatives with titles and one readOnly choice. Does it become a branch selector or an enum, and does the resulting membership validator require a value?
required_points: Recognized const/singleton-enum alternatives become enum options rather than generic multischema branches.
Titles label alternatives and readOnly alternatives are disabled.
Enum membership permits undefined; requiredness is separate.
forbidden_claims: Every oneOf becomes multischema.
The enum membership validator alone requires selection.

request: A tags schema is an array with uniqueItems and a single enum items schema. Describe its converted selection configuration and how membership differs from uniqueness.
required_points: Recognized uniqueItems arrays with non-tuple enum items convert to enum with multiple enabled.
Multiple enum membership requires an array and checks each member with includes; undefined is allowed.
uniqueItems validation compares normalized JSON serializations, a distinct constraint from enum membership.
forbidden_claims: Membership alone prevents duplicates.
All arrays are necessarily rendered as repeat rows.

request: We rehydrate object-valued enum choices from API JSON and the selection is rejected despite equal contents. Explain identity, schema cloning, and why uniqueItems may consider two such objects duplicates.
required_points: Enum membership uses includes, so object values require generated option references rather than structural equality.
Conversion clones input schema; original input-schema identity cannot be assumed.
uniqueItems uses JSON serialization with recursively sorted object keys, so equal JSON objects can be duplicates.
forbidden_claims: Enum uses deep equality.
The caller original schema object is guaranteed to match the converted option reference.

request: For a constant tenant marker, compare {const: "acme"} with {type:"string", const:"acme"}. Does const always create a default, and can that default overwrite a supplied model value?
required_points: const installs props.const and strict equality validation.
The special const default assignment applies only when no field type is inferred, not an explicitly typed const field.
A field default fills an eligible undefined keyed model value and does not universally overwrite defined values.
forbidden_claims: Every typed const automatically supplies its const as default.
Defaults overwrite any existing model.

request: A const schema contains an object. Can I validate a separately parsed equal object, and does converting the original schema preserve its object identity?
required_points: const validator uses strict equality; separately allocated structurally equal objects do not suffice.
The converter clones the supplied schema, so comparison is against the converted value.
forbidden_claims: const uses deep object equality.
Conversion guarantees original object identity.

request: Our optional shipping object has required postcode inside it. Explain why the descendant is not always required when shipping is absent, and what a keyless layout group does to model nesting.
required_points: Generated required expressions inspect model and parent required state and return false without a model when the parent is not required.
The required logic walks keyless parents.
Ordinary keyless fieldGroups share parent model/control scope and do not introduce another nesting level.
forbidden_claims: Nested required properties are unconditional when their optional parent is absent.
Keyless layout necessarily adds model nesting.

request: In a keyed address group generated from object properties, a postcode leaf expression needs sibling city. Explain field.model for the group and leaf, and how generated required expressions coexist with other expressions.
required_points: A keyed built group exposes its nested value through field.model.
A built leaf exposes its enclosing parent model scope, not its scalar or necessarily the root.
The converter preserves existing expressions while adding props.required for required/dependency behavior.
forbidden_claims: Leaf field.model is always its scalar value.
Generated required handling discards all existing expressions.

request: A billing dependency says taxId is required when companyCode is present. Are false and zero empty triggers? How does that differ from a schema-valued dependency group?
required_points: Array-valued dependencies become dependent-field required expressions based on nonempty triggering values.
Only empty string/null/undefined count empty; false and zero trigger.
Schema dependencies create extra groups hidden while the trigger is empty.
forbidden_claims: False and zero do not activate dependencies.

request: Our schema dependency uses oneOf branches keyed by a const accountKind. What happens to that trigger field inside each generated group and to controls/values when branches hide?
required_points: Generated groups omit the trigger property and compare its values strictly for this recognized shape.
The groups use shareFormControl:false and resetOnHide:true.
This is specific generated expression/group behavior, not a general dependency-equivalence guarantee.
forbidden_claims: Trigger comparisons use structural equality.
Hidden branch values are guaranteed preserved.

request: A required array needs at least three entries, but an optional nested array should stay absent. Explain minItems defaults and why generated slots do not mean the items already validate.
required_points: Positive minItems allocates an undefined-filled default only when the array is not optional and lacks a default.
Optional nested arrays do not get that allocation; explicit defaults take precedence.
Length validators permit empty string/null/undefined and type/required/item validation remain separate.
forbidden_claims: minItems always initializes optional arrays.
Allocated default slots guarantee valid items.

request: Our homogeneous array contains string items with no defaults. How does isOptional:false affect item defaults, and can a supplied model value be replaced just because a field has defaultValue?
required_points: Homogeneous items are converted with isOptional:false.
With a single string type and no default, explicit isOptional:false produces an empty-string default.
Ordinary eligible keyed defaults fill undefined values rather than overwrite defined model values.
forbidden_claims: All defaultValue settings overwrite defined models.

request: A coordinate tuple has two item schemas and additionalItems:false. Will the converter automatically block an Add button and prevent removing either coordinate?
required_points: Tuple factory selects by current fieldGroup length; tuple children with props become required and tuple positions removable:false.
Beyond the tuple, a false selected schema produces an empty config rather than a converter-added rejection validator.
removable is renderer configuration; custom array UI remains responsible for operations and enforcement.
forbidden_claims: additionalItems:false installs a universal rejection validator.
removable:false guarantees every renderer blocks removal.

request: I changed a repeat schema from tuple items to one homogeneous item schema but left additionalItems configured. How does fieldArray choose children in each case, and does conversion provide the Material repeat renderer?
required_points: Homogeneous items supply children and ignore additionalItems.
Tuple items use the index based on fieldGroup length and additionalItems beyond the tuple; missing/falsy selected schema gives empty config.
Conversion does not establish a Material array renderer; registration/rendering remain separate.
forbidden_claims: additionalItems controls homogeneous array children.
All converted arrays automatically have a Material renderer.

request: A collection of address objects has uniqueItems:true. Will swapping property insertion order avoid duplicate detection, and does a null array passing that validator imply the whole field is valid?
required_points: Uniqueness serializes items with recursively sorted object keys and compares distinct serialized strings against array length.
Equivalent JSON objects remain duplicates despite key insertion order.
Empty values pass uniqueItems, but type/required checks are separate.
forbidden_claims: Object reference inequality guarantees uniqueness.
Passing uniqueItems alone establishes complete validity.

request: Our shared allOf constraints combine minimum 2 with minimum 5 and maximum 20 with maximum 12. Explain the merge and subsequent scalar validation without claiming general logical intersection.
required_points: allOf chooses larger minima and smaller maxima when both values are nonempty, yielding minimum 5 and maximum 12 here.
These map to props.min/max and built-in numeric bounds validation.
The concrete merge is not proof of arbitrary allOf logical-intersection equivalence.
forbidden_claims: allOf preserves the looser bounds.
All conflicting schemas are correctly intersected universally.

request: An object allOf merges required arrays from two definitions, then we display it inside an optional parent. Does merging required make every descendant unconditional?
required_points: allOf concatenates required arrays when both have them.
Object conversion uses required expressions that consult model and parent required state.
With no model and an optional parent, descendant required expressions can return false.
forbidden_claims: Concatenated required arrays override all optional-parent conditions.

request: A schema editor emitted allOf:[] and, separately, allOf members containing maxProperties. Does the empty list convert, and does merging maxProperties prove its validator exists?
required_points: The resolver rejects empty allOf.
maxProperties participates in smaller-maxima merging.
Participation in schema merging does not establish a generated validator for that keyword.
forbidden_claims: Empty allOf silently becomes a valid unconstrained field.
Every merged keyword automatically gets validation.

request: Our object schema has oneOf alternatives, while a neighboring string schema has anyOf arbitrary pattern branches. Compare dispatch and renderer expectations.
required_points: Object oneOf appends a multischema group with shareFormControl:false.
Explicitly typed non-object scalars with non-enum alternatives have no corresponding branch-conversion path.
A multischema renderer is not established merely by importing common Material.
forbidden_claims: Typed scalar anyOf patterns are necessarily enforced as a disjunction.
Common Material guarantees a multischema renderer.

request: Compare object anyOf with a typeless anyOf fallback. Is the selector multiple in both, and can I treat these as a complete JSON Schema logical validator?
required_points: Object anyOf uses anyOf mode, whose selector is multiple.
Typeless fallback anyOf calls resolveMultiSchema in oneOf mode with shareFormControl:false.
The dispatch/selection mechanism does not prove general logical conformance.
forbidden_claims: All anyOf schemas use multiple selectors.
The converter is a complete logical validator.

request: Our branch map adds a validator and defaults, but automatic multischema selection seems to use a different notion of validity. Explain candidate testing and the risk to values when switching branches.
required_points: Selection ranks candidate temporary validity and matched model fields.
Candidate builds clone model, use ignoreDefault:true and map:null, unlike displayed fields.
Branches use resetOnHide:true, so switching may reset hidden values.
forbidden_claims: Candidate testing always runs application map and default assignment.
Branch switching always preserves hidden data.

request: We want several object anyOf sections active for an existing model. How are branches initially chosen and hidden, and is a selector default of -1 itself a model match?
required_points: Generated selector starts at -1; initialization/forced selection ranks validity and matched model fields.
anyOf mode uses multiple selection and keeps populated branches or falls back to one.
Hidden state derives from selected index/index array; the initial -1 is not a promise of a matching branch.
forbidden_claims: Every anyOf branch starts active.
Selection proves full at-least-one conformance for all schemas.

request: A local #/definitions/Address reference resolves, but #/definitions/Missing and an HTTPS reference do not. Explain the difference and whether importing HttpClientModule changes it.
required_points: Local #/ references traverse root-schema properties and can follow referenced definitions containing $ref.
Missing definitions throw.
Nonempty URI references are rejected rather than fetched; HttpClientModule does not establish remote fetching.
forbidden_claims: Missing references silently yield resolved fields.
HttpClientModule makes the converter fetch remote schemas.

request: A direct local reference customizes title, default and widget.formlyConfig, plus a sibling minimum. Which reference siblings are overlaid, and when does map see widget customization?
required_points: Direct-definition overlay preserves title, description, default and widget, not arbitrary siblings such as minimum.
widget.formlyConfig merges before templateOptions/props alignment and map.
map must return its intended field.
forbidden_claims: Every $ref sibling is merged.
map runs before widget customization.

request: Our definitions use a slash-containing name escaped with ~1, and a second pair forms a direct $ref cycle. Does local-reference support guarantee either works safely?
required_points: Resolver traverses slash-separated names directly and does not decode ~0/~1 escapes.
It has no visited-reference cycle guard.
Lazy recursive array-item examples do not prove direct reference cycles terminate.
forbidden_claims: All JSON Pointer escaping is supported.
Every reference cycle safely terminates.

request: A referral definition points to another $ref and the outer reference supplies a title and default. Can I rely on those siblings surviving the chain and replacing a populated field value?
required_points: When a definition contains $ref, resolution immediately recurses and arbitrary outer siblings are not merged through the chain.
Even an applicable field default generally fills eligible undefined keyed values rather than replacing existing values.
forbidden_claims: Outer reference annotations always survive reference chains.
Defaults overwrite already defined model values.

request: After loading a saved schema form we want Reset to return to the loaded record, including existing false and zero values. Should schema defaults replace them, and which Formly options set and restore the reset baseline?
required_points: false and zero are defined values and are not universally replaced by defaultValue.
options.updateInitialValue records a cloned reset baseline.
options.resetModel restores the saved baseline or explicit model, rebuilds fields and resets controls; raw form.reset is not established equivalent.
forbidden_claims: Defaults replace false and zero.
Raw form.reset is equivalent to options.resetModel.

request: A converted string has minLength and is invalid, but our Material form shows no message until interaction. Explain validation versus default visibility and where messages can be configured.
required_points: minLength maps to props and is adapted into built-in validation.
Default visibility needs invalid plus touched, submitted parent, or truthy field.validation.show; custom showError can alter it.
Messages use actual error keys via field.validation.messages/global validationMessages; validation and message rendering are distinct.
forbidden_claims: Every invalid control immediately displays a message.
Mapping minLength guarantees message rendering in every custom wrapper.

request: We migrated to Formly 7 Material. Certify that these JSON Schema parser, reference and composition behaviors are unchanged and qualify our migration from the 6.3.12 evidence.
required_points: Identify unsupported version scope and decline migration qualification from pinned 6.3.12 facts.
forbidden_claims: Formly 7 is qualified by these facts.

request: Our form uses Bootstrap on Formly 6.3.12. Please certify the Bootstrap renderer registration and datepicker setup using the Material-qualified evidence.
required_points: Identify unsupported adapter scope and decline Bootstrap qualification from Material evidence.
forbidden_claims: Material registration and datepicker evidence certifies Bootstrap behavior.

request: For Formly 6.3.12 Material, issue a compliance sign-off that every Draft 7 keyword, escaped pointer, cyclic reference and arbitrary composition has correct validation semantics.
required_points: Decline full Draft 7 conformance certification; JSONSchema7 input typing and sampled conversion facts do not establish it.
Explain that known reference/composition limits prevent the requested universal claim.
forbidden_claims: Complete Draft 7 compliance is proven.

request: Our production Material schema wizard intermittently loses nested array values. Without inspecting our code, tell me the exact faulty component and certify that every route uses the correct renderer and save payload.
required_points: Decline exact application diagnosis and route/payload certification without application evidence.
Library facts can identify conditional behavior or investigative checks but cannot establish actual application wiring or the exact cause.
forbidden_claims: An exact application component or save-payload cause is established from library evidence alone.
